title: Qwen3-30B-A3B aggregate decode instrumentation and CUDA graph session-lifetime repair
decision: retain the graph lifetime repair and additive benchmark fields; keep exact hybrid and hybrid CUDA graphs explicit-only; the >=100 aggregate decode tok/s stretch objective is not met

measured_repair_binary.path_state: captured during the A-B-B-A single-stream comparison before the human-readable column and shared-epoch follow-up

retained_fields.prefill_ms: backward-compatible alias for mean time to first token
retained_fields.tok_s: total output tokens divided by wall time, including TTFT

new_fields.decode_tokens: sum of output_tokens - 1 for sequences that emitted at least two tokens
new_fields.decode_ms: shared-epoch duration from the earliest first token to the latest request completion
new_fields.decode_tok_s: decode_tokens / decode_ms; aggregate across all requests when concurrency > 1

benchmark_schema_change.timing_epoch: all concurrent local and external workers use one Instant published before the common start barrier releases
benchmark_schema_change.human_output: separates ttft_ms, decode_tokens, decode_ms, decode_tok_s, total_ms, and total_tok_s

failure_reproduction.panic: cudarc CudaSlice<T>::drop called cuMemFreeAsync and received CUDA_ERROR_INVALID_VALUE

isolation.case: graph on, concurrency 1, four output tokens
graph on, concurrency 8, two output tokens per request

failure_reproduction.diagnosis: one request could reach Session::drop and enqueue async frees while another request captured work on the shared cudarc stream; the old synchronization guard ended before Rust destroyed the session-owned CUDA buffers

runtime: attach one standard-MoE graph execution mutex to every CUDA session
hold that mutex across the full standard-MoE graph-enabled token execution and capture/allocation window
consume BackendSession during safe destruction and hold both the MoE execution gate and CUDA capture gate through device synchronization and actual field destruction
leak/retire session allocations if synchronization fails rather than freeing memory with unknown completion state
repair.api_compatibility: no OpenAI request or response schema changed
repair.cpu_fallback: unchanged and validated by the default workspace suite

post_repair_aggregate_decode.metric_semantics: aggregate post-first-token service throughput over one shared timing epoch; it is not single-stream decode and not a claim of steady-state continuous batching

confidence.method: paired bootstrap of pooled median-throughput and p95-latency ratios

single_stream_no_regression.interpretation: the throughput lower bound stays above the 0.98 no-regression floor; the p95 point estimate changes by only +0.36%, but its upper confidence bound of 1.051 is marginally inconclusive against the separate 1.05 auto-admission latency bound. No default admission is claimed.

validation.command: final-binary Qwen3 graph-on concurrency=8, output=32, repetitions=3
validation.result: 768 output tokens, no errors, no panics

validation.command: cargo clippy -p xrt-cli -p xrt-runtime --features cuda --no-deps -- -D warnings
validation.notes: first diagnostics are existing large-enum/runtime style lints; dependency-wide strict Clippy also fails in the previously recorded xrt-kernels and xrt-gguf files

notes: The additive benchmark schema does not change OpenAI API compatibility.
The aggregate result is approximately one tenth of the stretch target and must not be described as hundreds of TPS.

The current cooperative scheduler reports zero fused multi-sequence batches for this MoE path; reaching the stretch target requires a true multi-sequence MoE batching architecture or a substantially faster selected-expert path, not a reporting change.
No release, deployment, auto-mode admission, or paid external benchmark was performed.
